issues.issue: Citations link to homepage-level URLs only, not specific pages or studies
issues.fix: Where possible, link to specific article, study, or page URLs rather than root domains (e.g., https://www.frontiersin.org/articles/... instead of https://www.frontiersin.org) to improve credibility and reduce risk of link rot perception

issues.issue: Only 10 inline citations used across the article; minimum target is 8-12 and distribution is uneven — several paragraphs have no citation
issues.fix: Add at least 1-2 more inline citations to uncited paragraphs, particularly the terpene bullet list section and the consumption method subsections, to reach a more even distribution and hit the upper end of the 8-12 target

issues.issue: Project CBD (source 6) is an advocacy organization, not a peer-reviewed or academic source, which slightly weakens the credibility mix
issues.fix: Consider replacing or supplementing with a peer-reviewed journal source specifically covering caryophyllene CB2 binding, such as a PubMed-indexed study, to strengthen the scientific credibility of the entourage effect and caryophyllene claims

issues.issue: Meta description is 154 characters, which is within range, but the keyword appears at the very end rather than near the beginning
issues.fix: Reorder the meta description to lead with or place the target keyword 'cannabis pharmacology explained' earlier — ideally within the first 60 characters — to improve keyword prominence in SERPs

issues.issue: No H3 subheadings are used anywhere in the article; all sections use H2 only
issues.fix: Introduce H3 subheadings within at least two H2 sections (e.g., under the THC/CBD section, add H3s for 'How THC Binds to CB1 Receptors' and 'How CBD Modulates the ECS') to deepen heading hierarchy and improve topical coverage for semantic SEO

issues.issue: No internal links are present in the article
issues.fix: Add 2-4 contextual internal links to related articles on the site (e.g., link 'terpene profiles' to a terpenes guide, or 'edibles' to a dosing article) to improve site architecture signals and reduce bounce rate

issues.issue: The claim that caryophyllene is 'the only terpene classified as a dietary cannabinoid' is accurate per current research but is based on limited and still-evolving science; it is stated as established fact without qualification
issues.fix: Add a brief qualifier such as 'according to current research' or 'as currently understood' to accurately reflect that this classification, while supported by studies, is not yet universally codified in regulatory or scientific consensus

issues.issue: The entourage effect is presented with moderate confidence, but scientific consensus on its magnitude and mechanisms remains debated in peer-reviewed literature
issues.fix: Add a brief caveat noting that while the entourage effect is a widely discussed concept, research is still ongoing and findings are not fully conclusive, to maintain scientific accuracy and reader trust

issues.issue: The conclusion is well-written but lacks a specific call-to-action directing the reader to another resource, tool, or next step on the site
issues.fix: Add a concrete CTA at the end of the conclusion, such as 'Browse our strain library with full terpene profiles' or 'Read our beginner's guide to cannabis dosing,' to improve engagement and time-on-site metrics

issues.issue: The image alt text is descriptive but does not fully match the target keyword format; it uses 'cannabis pharmacology explained: THC and CBD molecular structures...' which is good but could be tightened
issues.fix: Ensure the alt text leads cleanly with the target keyword and is concise: e.g., 'Cannabis pharmacology explained — diagram of THC and CBD interactions with brain CB1 receptors'
